knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186083243/outputs-0/curve-262315be0f881f43c6105311.png)

For the parametric curve 

$$
x=t^{3} + 2 t^{2},\,y=2 t^{2},\,-\infty<t<\infty,
$$

shown above, calculate the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=3.$ Do not round the answer.

$m=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=3 t^{2} + 4 t,\,y'(t)=4 t.
$$

 

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(4 t\right)}{\left(3 t^{2} + 4 t\right)} \\  & =\frac{4}{3 t + 4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=3,$ the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{dy}{dx}\,{|}_{t=3} & =\frac{4}{3 \left(3\right) + 4} \\  & =\frac{4}{13} \\  & =\frac{4}{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=4 \sin {t},\,y=\frac{6 t^{2}}{\pi},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{3 \pi}{4}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=4 \cos {t},\,y'(t)=\frac{12 t}{\pi}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(\frac{12 t}{\pi}\right)}{\left(4 \cos {t}\right)} \\  & =\frac{3 t \sec {t}}{\pi}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{3 \pi}{4},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{3 \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right) \sec {\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)}}{\pi} \\  & =\frac{3 \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right) \left(- \sqrt{2}\right)}{\pi} \\  & =- \frac{9 \sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=5 t^{3} + 1,\,y=4 t^{4} + 3 t^{2},\,0\le t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=15 t^{2},\,y'(t)=2 t \left(8 t^{2} + 3\right).
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(2 t \left(8 t^{2} + 3\right)\right)}{\left(15 t^{2}\right)} \\  & =\frac{2 \left(8 t^{2} + 3\right)}{15 t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=3,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{2 \left(8 \left(3\right)^{2} + 3\right)}{15 \left(3\right)} \\  & =\frac{150}{45} \\  & =\frac{10}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=5 \sin {2 t},\,y=\cos^{2} {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi}{6}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=10 \cos {2 t},\,y'(t)=- 2 \sin {t} \cos {t}=- \sin {2 t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- \sin {2 t}\right)}{\left(10 \cos {2 t}\right)} \\  & =- \frac{\tan {2 t}}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{\pi}{6},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{\tan {2 \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)}}{10} \\  & =- \frac{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)}{10} \\  & =- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.

x'(t)=10 \cos {2 t},\,y'(t)=12 \sin {t} \cos {t}=6 \sin {2 t}.

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=2 t + \sin {t},\,y=t + \cos {t},\,0\le t<2\pi,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=\cos {t} + 2,\,y'(t)=1 - \sin {t}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(1 - \sin {t}\right)}{\left(\cos {t} + 2\right)} \\  & =\frac{1 - \sin {t}}{\cos {t} + 2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{\pi}{2},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{1 - \sin {\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}}{\cos {\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)} + 2} \\  & =\frac{1 - \left(1\right)}{\left(0\right) + 2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=2 t^{2} + 3,\,y=3 t^{5} + t^{3},\,0\le t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=4 t,\,y'(t)=3 t^{2} \left(5 t^{2} + 1\right).
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(3 t^{2} \left(5 t^{2} + 1\right)\right)}{\left(4 t\right)} \\  & =\frac{3 t \left(5 t^{2} + 1\right)}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=1,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{3 \left(1\right) \left(5 \left(1\right)^{2} + 1\right)}{4} \\  & =\frac{18}{4} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{t}},\,y=\frac{e^{t}}{2 t},\,0<t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{1}{4 t^{\frac{3}{2}}},\,y'(t)=\frac{2 t e^{t} - 2 e^{t}}{4 t^{2}}=\frac{\left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{2 t^{2}}.
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{2 t^{2}}\cdot \left(- 4 t^{\frac{3}{2}}\right) \\  & =- \frac{2 \left(t - 1\right) e^{t}}{\sqrt{t}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=1,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{2 \left(\left(1\right) - 1\right) e^{\left(1\right)}}{\sqrt{\left(1\right)}} \\  & =\frac{0}{1} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=\sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}},\,y=\cot{\left(e^{t} \right)},\,-\infty<t<1,
$$

calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x'(t)&=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}\cdot \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}\cdot e^{t}\\ &= \frac{e^{t} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}},\\ y'(t)&=- e^{t} \csc^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- e^{t} \csc^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)}\right)}{\left(\frac{e^{t} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}{2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{- 2 \sqrt{\sin{\left(e^{t} \right)}}}{\sin^{2}{\left(e^{t} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}} \\  & =- \frac{2}{\sin^{\frac{3}{2}}{\left(e^{t} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{t} \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{2}{\sin^{\frac{3}{2}}{\left(e^{\left(\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\right)} \right)} \cos{\left(e^{\left(\ln{\left(\frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\right)} \right)}} \\  & =\frac{-2}{1\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)} \\  & =- \frac{8 \sqrt{6}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- 3 \cot {t} \csc^{3} {t}\right)}{\left(2 \tan {t} \sec^{2} {t}\right)} \\  & =- 3 \cot {t} \csc^{3} {t}\left(\frac{\cos^{2} {t} \cot {t}}{2}\right) \\  & =- \frac{3}{2}\,\cos^{2} {t} \cot^{2} {t} \csc^{3} {t} \\  & =- \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{1}{\sin^{3} {t}}\right)\left(\frac{\cos^{2} {t}}{\sin^{2} {t}}\right)\cos^{2} {t} \\  & =- \frac{3 \cos^{4} {t}}{2 \sin^{5} {t}} \\  & =- \frac{3 \cot^{4} {t} \csc {t}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=\frac{\pi}{4},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =- \frac{3 \cot^{4} {\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)} \csc {\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-3\cdot \left(\sqrt{2}\right)\cdot \left(1\right)^{4}}{2} \\  & =- \frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
